title: Accuracy of planned versus achieved tooth movement using thermoformed and 3D-printed aligners in adult patients: randomized controlled trial
summary: Clear aligners (often called “invisible braces”) are becoming very popular. They can be made in two main ways: by heating and shaping plastic over a model of the teeth (thermoforming), or by 3D printing the aligner directly. Both methods can be used to produce the appliance and straighten teeth, but they may differ in how well the aligners fit, how stiff they are, and how they push on the teeth. These differences could change how closely the teeth end up in the positions planned by the orthodontist. So far, there has not been a high-quality study which compares the two methods. In this study, adult patients are assigned to one method or the other by chance and the results are compared.

interventions.name: Orthodontic treatment of the malocclusion with one series of 3D printed Aligners
Orthodontic treatment of the malocclusion with one series of thermoformed Aligners

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
signed informed consent, capacity to consent.
Indication for orthodontic treatment with aligners.
Mild to moderate malocclusion.
Exclusion criteria:
Craniofacial anomalies.
Complex malocclusions, extraction therapy required as part of treatment.
Systemic diseases (acute or chronic).
Oral pathologies (e.g., active caries, gingivitis or periodontitis)
